sections.normalized_html:
First, we rewrite the given line in slope-intercept form to find its slope:

[MATH: -3x + y = 5 \quad \implies \quad y = 3x + 5]

So, the slope of line [MATH: p] is [MATH: 3.]

A line perpendicular to this line will have slope [MATH: -\dfrac{1}{3},] since the slopes of perpendicular lines are negative reciprocals.

The perpendicular line must pass through [MATH: (0, -4).] So its equation in slope-intercept form is

[MATH: y = -\frac{1}{3}x - 4.]

To write this in standard form, we multiply both sides by 3 and rearrange:

[MATH: x + 3y = -12]

Therefore, an equation of line [MATH: q] is [MATH: x + 3y = -12.]

So, the slopes of the lines are [MATH: -\dfrac{a}{b}] and [MATH: -\dfrac{2}{9},] respectively.

The slopes of perpendicular lines are negative reciprocals. The reciprocal of [MATH: -\dfrac{2}{9}] is [MATH: -\dfrac{9}{2},] and changing the sign gives:

[MATH: -\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{9}{2} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \dfrac{b}{a} = -\dfrac{2}{9}.]

Therefore, [MATH: \dfrac{b}{a} = -\dfrac{2}{9}.]

Now, a line is perpendicular to another line when its slope is the negative reciprocal of that other line's slope. That means the second line must have slope [MATH: -\dfrac{1}{4}.]

From the line equation [MATH: mx + ny = 1,] it follows that the slope of the second line is [MATH: -\dfrac{m}{n}.] So we set [MATH: -\dfrac{m}{n} = -\dfrac{1}{4} \quad \Rightarrow \quad \dfrac{m}{n} = \dfrac{1}{4}]

Now, let's utilise this information to check which pair of lines is perpendicular:

  • First, we consider the following lines: [MATH: 4x + y = 1|⇒y = − 4x + 1; mx + 2ny = 1|⇒y = − (m)/(2n)x + (1)/(2n)] The slope of the first line is [MATH: -4.] The slope of the second line is [MATH: − (m)/(2n)|= − (1)/(2) ⋅ (m)/(n); = − (1)/(2) ⋅ (1)/(4); = − (1)/(8).] Since the product of slopes does not equal [MATH: -1,] this pair of lines is NOT perpendicular.

  • Next, we consider the following lines: [MATH: 4x + y = 1|⇒y = − 4x + 1; mx − ny = 1|⇒y = (m)/(n)x − (1)/(n)] The slope of the first line is [MATH: -4.] The slope of the second line is [MATH: \dfrac m n = \dfrac 1 4.] Since the product of the slopes equals [MATH: -1,] this pair of lines is perpendicular.

  • Finally, we consider the following lines: [MATH: 8x − 2y = 1|⇒y = 4x − (1)/(2); 2mx + ny = 1|⇒y = − (2m)/(n)x + (1)/(n)] The slope of the first line is [MATH: 4.] The slope of the second line is [MATH: − (2m)/(n)|= − 2 ⋅ (m)/(n); = − 2 ⋅ (1)/(4); = − (1)/(2)] Since the product of slopes does not equal [MATH: -1,] this pair of lines is NOT perpendicular.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
